title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 21
description: Ten questions on Exodus 21: the laws about servants, violence, injuries and goring bulls.

questions.text: How many years was a bought Hebrew servant to serve before going out free?
questions.explanation: A Hebrew servant was to serve six years, and in the seventh he would go out free without paying anything.

answers.text: Six years
Three years
Ten years
Twelve years

questions.text: If a master gave his servant a wife and she bore him children, what happened when the servant went free?
questions.explanation: The wife and her children would be her master's, and the servant would go out by himself.

answers.text: They all went out with him
They were sold to another master
They paid a price to go with him
The wife and children stayed with the master

questions.text: With what did the master bore the ear of a servant who chose to stay?
questions.explanation: The master brought him to the door or doorpost and bored his ear through with an awl, and he served him forever.

answers.text: A nail
An awl
A knife
A needle

questions.text: Which three things may a master not take away from a female servant he married when he takes another wife?
questions.explanation: He shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights; if he does not do these three things, she may go free.

answers.text: Her land, her house and her cattle
Her silver, her gold and her jewels
Her food, her clothing and her marital rights
Her bread, her wine and her oil

questions.text: What would God appoint for someone who killed a man unintentionally?
questions.explanation: If it was unintentional, God says: 'I will appoint you a place where he shall flee.'

answers.text: A fine paid in silver
Death by stoning
Seven years as a servant
A place where he could flee

questions.text: If a man was injured in a quarrel but got up and walked with his staff, what did the one who struck him have to do?
questions.explanation: He was cleared, but he had to pay for the loss of the man's time and provide for his healing until he was thoroughly healed.

answers.text: Pay for his lost time and his healing
Pay him double what he lost
Give him an ox from his herd
Serve him as a servant for six years

questions.text: What must a man do if he strikes his servant's eye and destroys it?
questions.explanation: He shall let the servant go free for his eye's sake.

answers.text: Pay a fine to the judges
Give the servant a field
Let the servant go free
Be put to death

questions.text: What happens to a bull that gores a man or a woman to death?
questions.explanation: The bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; the owner is not held responsible.

answers.text: It is sold and the money given to the family
It is stoned and its meat is not eaten
It is offered on the altar
It is given to the priest

questions.text: How much silver was to be given to the master if a bull gored his servant?
questions.explanation: Thirty shekels of silver were to be given to their master, and the ox was to be stoned.

answers.text: Thirty shekels
Ten shekels
Twenty shekels
Fifty shekels

questions.text: If one man's bull kills another man's bull, what are they to do?
questions.explanation: They shall sell the live bull and divide its price, and they shall also divide the dead animal.

answers.text: Let the owner of the live bull keep both
Stone the live bull as well
Offer the live bull as a sacrifice
Sell the live bull and divide its price
